title: Your mates give the puck back: a mate with the puck passes to the open human in 0.8 of the chances at every level (thirdjam: 0.6 / 0.4 / 0.2)
pillar: P2 the pass is the fastest thing on the ice, and it gets there (the pass must pay through the mates: no control switching, R-0038)
hypothesis: A completed pass is half lost: of the planning hand's completed passes at pro on hockey.regular, 55 % are followed first by an opponent carrying the puck, 39 % come back to the human, 5 % become a mate's shot. In a game where you are one skater, a pass pays when it comes back to you in a better place (the give-and-go) or becomes a shot. thirdjam's mates return the puck to an open human (on his feet, 5 to 25 m away, ahead of or level with the puck, the lane free) in a share of the two-second windows that FALLS with the level: 0.6 at rookie, 0.4 at pro, 0.2 at all-star (DifficultyProfile.cpp: MatesPassShare; JamAICore.cpp:1675-1690). That makes a level harder by your own mates' absence, which the owner ruled out (R-0067: 'a level is easy by clumsiness, never by absence'), and it makes the pass a gift. The change: 0.8 at every level (the signal 'pass' already sets 0.9 for a moment: the rule and its geometry are thirdjam's own). Expected: more of the completed passes come back (39 % toward 55 %), fewer are lost; passes received a match up; taking the pass away costs the planning hand (T3); the one-timer a little more often. Risk: PLAY 2d held the 'pass' signal all match and the scripted hand lost 13 points at pro; that signal also lets the backs pass and was read through a hand that does not go to open ice, so it is a warning, not a forecast.
tempo: none: no row of the tempo map moves

why: The number is not what holds the puck back: doubling it changed almost nothing. For thirdjam's regular hand at pro all 60 matches ended as before (paired 0.0 +-0; goal difference 0.00 +-0.02); for the planning hand the same at pro (0.0 +-0 at all three settings) and -1.7 +-1.7 at all-star. Of the planning hand's completed passes at pro 36.4 % came back before and 35.5 % after; passes received a match 4.9 and 5.0. The mates' coin is rarely tossed: the conditions in front of it (the human on his feet 5 to 25 m away, ahead of or level with the puck, his lane free, the mate not driving the net) are what decide, and the share only scales the few windows that pass them. No target moved, so it is not kept (a change that does nothing is a decoration).
notes: What it taught: making the pass pay through the mates is not a level number. It needs the mates' behaviour itself: what a mate does in the first second after the human's pass reaches him (he is stripped or hit in 49 to 62 % of the cases before anything comes of it), and when he looks for the human again. That is a patch to the brain's copy in the thirdlife tree (thirdjam's AI files stay byte for byte), with its own switch: round 3. Epoch k8-4 (the repaired hand).
